title: Formula fields and cross-object formulas
objectives: Define a formula field as a custom field whose value is calculated from other fields, with a chosen return type.
Use a cross-object formula to read fields on a related parent through lookup or master-detail, instead of stamping a stored copy.
State the official maximum of 10 unique relationships per object across formula fields, rules, and lookup filters.
Refuse formula fields that should be roll-up summaries, validation rules, or editable stored fields.
diagnostic_question: Users want Property's city on every inspection, a count of inspections on the property, and a block if city is blank. Which of those is a formula field, which is not, and why?
definition: A formula field is a custom field that calculates a value from other fields or expressions and stores a return type such as text, number, currency, percent, date, date/time, or checkbox. A cross-object formula references fields on a related parent through a lookup or master-detail relationship. Salesforce allows a maximum of 10 unique relationships per object in cross-object formulas, cumulative across formula fields, rules, and lookup filters. You cannot reference cross-object formulas in roll-up summary fields. ([Tips for Building Cross-Object Formulas](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm); [Formula Field Limits and Restrictions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.formula_field_limits.htm); [Formula Operators and Functions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.usefulFormulaFields.meta/usefulFormulaFields/customize_functions.htm))
why_it_matters: Teams stamp parent city into a text field and then wonder why it goes stale. A formula field is the calculated display. Interviewers also listen for the 10 unique-relationship limit and for not using a formula to count children—that is a roll-up or automation alternative.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a store receipt reprint. The line-item prices are stored fields. The reprint total is calculated every time you look—you do not pencil it in. A cross-object formula is reading the store name from the receipt header. You get ten unique header walks per object across formulas, rules, and lookup filters. You cannot feed that reprint formula into a roll-up tally on the header.
deeper_explanation: Formula fields are a custom field data type (DATA-002). You choose a return type. Users do not type the value; the platform calculates it from referenced fields and functions. Formula operators and functions are shared with validation rules and other formula contexts, with some functions limited by context. ([Formula Operators and Functions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.usefulFormulaFields.meta/usefulFormulaFields/customize_functions.htm); [Custom Field Attributes](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.custom_field_attributes.htm))

Cross-object formulas walk lookup or master-detail relationships to parent fields. Two formulas on Opportunity that both reference Account count as one unique relationship (Opportunity to Account). The maximum of 10 unique relationships per object is cumulative across formula fields, rules, and lookup filters. ([Tips for Building Cross-Object Formulas](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm))

You cannot reference cross-object formulas in roll-up summary fields. You cannot directly reference some parent aggregate fields (for example GrandTotal on Quote) in formula fields; Help suggests roll-up summaries to aggregate children instead. Polymorphic fields such as Case Owner require an object type qualifier. ([Tips for Building Cross-Object Formulas](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.fields_creating_cross_object_notes.htm); [Formula Field Limits and Restrictions](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.formula_field_limits.htm))

Compile-size and other numeric formula limits exist and are release-sensitive—Needs verification of the current compile-size number in Formula Field Limits before quoting it. Activity merge-field restrictions and Profile.Name list-view quirks are documented in the cross-object tips; do not invent extra ones.

A formula field is not a validation rule (DATA-010), not a roll-up of children (DATA-007), and not an editable stored field. It is a good selective-denormalization alternative (DATA-005) because the platform is the writer.

mental_model.analogy: A store receipt reprint: stored line prices are typed fields; the reprint total and store header name are calculated when you look, not penciled in.
useful_mapping: formula field → reprint line that recalculates
return type → currency, text, checkbox, and so on of that reprint
cross-object formula → reading the store name from the header
unique relationship → one header walk, even if two formulas read two header fields
10 unique relationships → ten header walks per object across formulas, rules, and lookup filters
stored stamp → penciling the store name on every line (goes stale)
roll-up → tallying lines onto the header (not a formula on the line)
where_it_breaks: Formula compile size is not a paper receipt limit; look up current Help before quoting a number.
Formulas do not query arbitrary child sets; that is roll-up or automation.
Polymorphic Owner walks need a type qualifier the receipt analogy does not show.
Formula values are not always stored columns you can index like a custom text field—Needs verification of current index/filter behavior for your use case.

teach_back_prompt: Explain a formula field versus a stored custom field, then a cross-object formula versus a roll-up, and state the 10 unique-relationship rule.

telugu_glossary.telugu: A calculated custom field users do not type.
A formula that reads a related parent field.
One parent walk, even if several formulas use it.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A formula field calculates a return type from other fields. A cross-object formula reads a parent through lookup or master-detail. You get 10 unique relationships per object across formulas, rules, and lookup filters. Formulas do not count children; roll-ups do. Do not stamp parent city in text.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick formula when the value should always match its inputs. I walk Account.BillingCity from Inspection via the property relationship if we are under the unique-relationship cap. I refuse formula for child counts and for blocking saves—that is roll-up or validation. I mention polymorphic Owner needs a type. I do not quote compile size unless I have the current Help number.

terminology.precise: A custom field whose value is defined by a formula and a return type. Users do not type it.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Default value formula: fills a stored field on create; not the same as a formula field.
terminology.boundary: Functions are shared with other formula contexts.

terminology.plain: The data type of the calculated result.
terminology.precise: Chosen when you create the formula field: text, number, currency, percent, date, date/time, or checkbox, as the type catalog allows.
terminology.non_example: The types of the input fields if they differ from the return.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Roll-up type COUNT/SUM: a different field type (DATA-007).
terminology.boundary: Return type drives reporting, same as DATA-002.

terminology.plain: A formula that reads a related parent.
terminology.precise: References merge fields on records related through lookup or master-detail.
terminology.non_example: A stored City__c stamp on Inspection.

terminology.plain: One parent walk, however many fields you read.
terminology.precise: Two Opportunity formulas referencing two Account fields still count as one unique relationship (Opportunity to Account).
terminology.example: Account.Name and Account.Industry in two Opportunity formulas = one relationship.
terminology.non_example: Ten different parent objects referenced = ten relationships.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lookup filter: also consumes the same cumulative cap.
terminology.boundary: Maximum 10 per object across formulas, rules, and lookup filters.

terminology.plain: The field token you insert into a formula.
terminology.precise: A reference such as Account.Name or Property__r.City__c used in the formula editor.
terminology.non_example: A page-layout field just sitting on the layout.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: API name: the merge field uses the API name.
terminology.boundary: Polymorphic merges may need a type qualifier.

terminology.plain: Another name for walking related records.
terminology.precise: Formula Field Limits: formula fields and rules can reference related records through lookup or master-detail; record-type default-value formulas cannot span the same way.
terminology.example: Opportunity validation formula reading Account fields.
terminology.non_example: Record-type default that tries to read another object—restricted.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Roll-up: aggregates children, does not span upward.
terminology.boundary: Keep defaults vs formula fields distinct.

terminology.plain: A relationship that can point at more than one object type.
terminology.precise: Case Owner can be User or Group; Owner.Email without a type qualifier errors: specify an object type.
terminology.non_example: Account.Name on Opportunity, which is not polymorphic.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lookup to a single object: ordinary cross-object.
terminology.boundary: Visualforce Owner references have extra documented limits.

terminology.plain: A named operation in the formula language.
terminology.precise: Operators and functions documented by context; most work in formula fields, validation rules, and other formula sites unless specified.
terminology.example: TEXT(), ISBLANK(), AND() in a formula field.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: VLOOKUP: Help says it is only available in validation rules, not formula fields.

interview_questions.question: What is a formula field, and when do you use a cross-object formula?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A formula field calculates a return type from other fields. A cross-object formula reads a parent through lookup or master-detail so you do not stamp a stale copy.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I contrast stored fields, formulas, roll-ups, and validation. I mention the 10 unique-relationship cap that also counts rules and lookup filters. I give the Opportunity-Account example where two fields are still one relationship. I do not quote compile size without current Help.
interview_questions.example: LAB_PropertyCity__c formula on Inspection reading Property__r.LAB_City__c.
follow_ups: What counts as a unique relationship?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling every calculated value a roll-up

interview_questions.question: Show Account industry on Opportunity without a text field. How?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A cross-object formula on Opportunity referencing Account.Industry. That is one unique relationship to Account, even if another formula already reads Account.Name.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I refuse Opportunity.IndustryCopy__c text. I check how many unique walks Opportunity already uses. I set return type Text. I add FLS and the layout. I note list views and reports can use the formula. I do not use this to block saves.
tradeoffs: Reuse Account walk vs new parent walk
follow_ups: What if we need Industry on a roll-up?
weak_answer_warnings: Creating a text field updated by workflow thinking

interview_questions.question: They want a formula on Account that counts open cases. Your answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A formula field cannot aggregate children. Use a roll-up summary if the relationship is master-detail, or a DATA-007 alternative if it is lookup.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain direction: formulas walk up; roll-ups tally down. I mention Help forbids putting cross-object formulas into roll-ups, which is the opposite mistake. I do not invent a COUNT() child function in a formula field. I also refuse VLOOKUP as a case counter.
interview_questions.example: Rejected Account.OpenCaseCount__c formula; proposed roll-up or Flow/Apex alternative.
follow_ups: What if Case is lookup to Account?

interview_questions.question: Explain the 10 unique-relationship limit.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Each object may use at most 10 unique relationships in cross-object formulas. The cap is cumulative across formula fields, rules, and lookup filters. Multiple fields on the same parent count as one relationship.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use the Opportunity-Account Help example. I audit existing formulas, validation rules, and lookup filters before adding a new parent walk. If we are at 10, I reuse a walk or move logic. I do not say 10 per field.
interview_questions.example: Opportunity already spans Account and several custom lookups; a new walk is rejected until we free a relationship.
tradeoffs: Reuse a walk vs new object
follow_ups: Do approval rules count? The article says rules—confirm type.
Do workflow rules still count in this org?
weak_answer_warnings: Treating the cap as 10 formula fields

interview_questions.question: A roll-up cannot use your inspection city formula. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If that formula is cross-object, Help says you cannot reference cross-object formulas in roll-up summary fields.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I check whether LAB_PropertyCity__c spans Property. If yes, the roll-up must aggregate a stored or same-object field instead. I do not change the roll-up operation from SUM to MAX expecting the ban to lift. I might store city on the child only if we accept denormalization with a writer—usually we keep the formula for display and roll up something else.
interview_questions.example: Roll-up on Property cannot SUM a spanning city formula on Inspection.
tradeoffs: Stamp city to roll it up vs do not roll up city
follow_ups: Can a same-object formula be rolled up? Needs verification.

interview_questions.question: Formula field versus validation rule versus stored field—how do you choose?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Stored if users edit it. Formula if it must always match inputs. Validation if a save must fail. The title words matter: a formula field is a field, not an error message.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use the city example: display city with a formula; require city with a validation rule on the object that owns city; do not make inspectors type city. I mention default-value formulas are another stored-field feature and do not span like formula fields. I keep Flow out unless the others cannot do it.
interview_questions.example: Property validation requires city; Inspection formula displays it; no stored copy.

interview_questions.question: A Case formula on Owner.Email asks you to specify an object type. What do you do?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Owner is polymorphic. Qualify the merge field with an object type, such as Owner:User.Email, instead of Owner.Email.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite the cross-object tips error. I do not remove the email field from User. I check whether the owner can be a queue/group and whether the formula should use a different field if queues matter. Visualforce Owner references have extra documented limits I will not invent beyond that note.

interview_questions.question: How do formula fields support schema design without denormalizing badly?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A cross-object formula lets the child display a parent fact while the source of truth stays on the parent. That is calculated display, not a second stored truth.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: DATA-005 said stamp only with a writer. The platform is the writer for a formula field. I still watch the 10 unique-relationship budget and I still refuse formulas that try to aggregate children. I mention compile-size as Needs verification rather than a memorized number.
